realComponents: Nest TestingModule provider construction, initialization, close and reconstruction

verifiedBehaviors: Two reply segments are frozen before dispatch and retain stable external request IDs across service reconstruction.
Provider acceptance alone leaves the first segment unconfirmed; recovery records unknown without dispatching again or acknowledging the input.
Callbacks with mismatched token, account, chat, request ID or text do not complete the action.
Duplicate exact callbacks do not create additional callback evidence or repeat dispatch.
Exact callback evidence is consumed by ActionRecovery; ReplyRecovery then dispatches only the remaining frozen segment.
Existing execute plans retain execute semantics after reconstruction in observe mode.
The group route resolves a rotated current credential without storing either credential in the persisted recovery payload.
Both segments finish succeeded with complete local synchronization; the durable turn becomes acked.
The actual workflow calls acknowledgement and deduplication for the original input only; the simulated later pending input remains.
The model boundary is invoked once; recovery reuses the persisted reply.
Replaying the original input after account migration to another group does not dispatch the remaining segment or acknowledge the turn.
simulatedBoundariesAndLimits: Provider HTTP send responses and callback bodies are synthetic. No Stride or WeCom messages were sent.
The trusted group directory is supplied by a mocked global fetch response, while the actual credential resolver parses and validates it.
Redis lease, pending-message storage and deduplication are test doubles. Actual Redis execution, ACK Lua behavior, Redis durability and distributed locking are not validated by this suite.
The controller is invoked directly inside Nest; the deployed HTTP listener, ingress proxy and middleware are not validated.
Restart means closing and reconstructing the Nest TestingModule while preserving external fixture state, not restarting the application OS process.
The actual PostgreSQL server-restart drill belongs to the separate SQL acceptance; this suite does not restart PostgreSQL.
Model output and unrelated business side effects are simulated.
This result does not establish real platform callback shape, delivery reliability, credential-directory availability or production readiness.

reasoning: The sole production persistedMode call site first rejects any parent reply turn whose stored mode is not execute.

Inherited execute is used for preparing a new child and for all enforcement decisions; missing cutover, unreliable identity, database failure or an absent/non-execute action row blocks before dispatch.

Existing observation action records are not promoted into execute. Existing execute succeeded/executing/unknown/cancelled/nonretryable-failed records retain their existing result rather than invoking dispatch again.
Claim conflicts, ownership expiry and ownership-query failure remain fail-closed. SQL serializes the resource and retains the immutable action mode and registered request ID.
Both request dispatch and recovery continue to use the registered execute request ID; unknown results stop the reply before any later segment.
